title: Paloma and the Drop
premise: Ulyana Pemberton, an interpreter who quietly handles deniable work for failing peace talks, notices that Flight 447 to Frankfurt has been erased from every system while still airborne—yet he spoke with someone aboard minutes earlier. The vanished flight carried 'the Drop,' a sealed inheritance of blackmail material that three governments will kill to bury, and its only living witness is a woman calling herself Paloma, who may be the courier, the assassin, or both. As Ulyana smuggles her testimony across borders before markets open in Frankfurt, he discovers his own erased past was manufactured by the same machine that deleted the flight. In the end, Ulyana chooses exposure over survival, broadcasting the truth at market open—and learns Paloma engineered the whole crisis to force him, the one interpreter she trusted, into becoming the witness she could never be.
about_author: Bram Kavanagh spent eleven years as a contract translator for diplomatic missions across Eastern Europe before turning to fiction, a career he describes as 'learning what people say when they mean something else.' He writes from a coastal town in Portugal and refuses interviews conducted in any language he speaks fluently.

chapters.title: The Language of No One
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At a collapsing Geneva peace summit, Ulyana interprets a threat no principal will put on record, establishing his role as the man who carries words no one wants attributed. A stranger named Paloma watches him from the gallery and leaves him a note in a dialect that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: quiet professional loneliness cracked by recognition—he's being recruited, or hunted.

chapters.title: Flight 447, Still Airborne
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Boarding data for Flight 447 to Frankfurt evaporates mid-flight: manifests, radar logs, even his own call records with a passenger contact. Yet he remembers the voice. His handler denies everything with rehearsed smoothness. Emotional beat: vertigo—the first hint that memory itself can be edited by people with power.

chapters.title: Paloma
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, first time. She surfaces in a Trieste safehouse, wounded, carrying a case containing 'the Drop'—an inherited archive of leverage over all three delegations. She tests Ulyana by feeding him a false detail and watching where it travels. Emotional beat: wary mutual need; two people whose professions are built on not being believed.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Liar
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Chased through Trieste's old quarter by men with diplomatic plates, Ulyana realizes each government blames the other two for the deletion—a perfect triangle of plausible denial. He decodes the Drop's index and finds his own birth name listed among the fabricated identities. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She reveals the Drop was assembled by her father, a broker of secrets who willed it to whoever proved willing to burn it rather than sell it. Ulyana is her inheritance test. Flashbacks show her childhood inside the archive trade. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; power as a family disease.

chapters.title: Overnight Train to Basel
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The pair moves by rail while assassins close in; Ulyana uses interpreter tradecraft—accent mimicry, forged credentials—to pass checkpoints. A near-capture forces them to trust each other completely. Emotional beat: intimacy under pressure; the strange honesty of two professional liars with nothing left to perform for.

chapters.title: What the Markets Know
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In Basel, a financier offers Ulyana wealth and erasure if he sells the Drop before Frankfurt opens, revealing the deletion wasn't concealment but positioning—a short against three currencies. Ulyana understands the flight never mattered; the fear did. Emotional beat: clarity—the corruption isn't hidden, it's priced in.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Terms
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The assassin pursuing them turns out to be her father's former protégé, bound by the same inheritance law: he may claim the Drop only by taking it from a willing heir. He offers Paloma a clean death and a clean story. Emotional beat: dread and temptation; the elegant horror of rules designed by monsters.

chapters.title: Open
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. At 8:00 a.m. CET, Ulyana walks into the Frankfurt exchange press gallery and interprets the Drop aloud—in four languages, live, unattributable to any government because it belongs to everyone. The assassin holds fire, bound by the terms; Paloma watches from the crowd. Emotional beat: terror becoming triumph as speech becomes the one weapon no one can delete.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Unattached
chapters.summary: Shared POV, resolution. Markets convulse, resignations cascade, and Ulyana—now unemployable and finally free—meets Paloma one last time. She leaves him the empty case and a single true sentence about who she really was. He burns his own file. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; identity chosen rather than assigned, inheritance refused rather than claimed.
